A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, A Recovery Guarantee for Sparse Neural Networks. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite relocated sections and added analyses.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original IHT-versus-IMP experiments on planted-MLP recovery, MNIST classification, and implicit representations of MNIST and CIFAR-10 images.

after.justification: Section 5 retains those original experiments. Appendix B additionally reports update-frequency and convergence experiments, plus variability for the retained results.

M1.justification: The IHT updates, sequential convex procedure, count sketching, acceleration and deeper-network adaptation remain unchanged. The update-frequency sweep is an ablation; the suggested stopping criterion is explicitly not used in the main experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same planted-MLP, MNIST classification and MNIST/CIFAR-10 representation tasks. The new sensitivity experiment stays within the existing scalar-output planted-MLP task.

E2.justification: IMP remains the comparison baseline in Figures 1–5. Appendix B compares IHT update schedules without adding or removing an external comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds a controlled 100-step experiment with input dimension 100, hidden dimension 10 and sparsity 500, sweeping selected sensing-matrix update intervals from 1 to 100. It also extends the interval-5 run beyond 100 steps. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Tables 1–2 test how update frequency affects fitting quality and sensing-matrix support stabilization. This adds a focused sensitivity and convergence analysis at one planted-MLP configuration, absent from v1.

E5.justification: Where v1 reports averages over three random trials, v2 adds standard-deviation heatmaps for every experiment represented in Figures 1–5 through new Figures 6–10. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting across the empirical suite; the stated trial count remains three.

E6.justification: The original performance heatmaps and runtime examples are unchanged. New Table 1 reports PSNR 161.44 for update intervals 1–4, 36.63 for interval 5 and 19.88 for interval 100. Table 2 reports support stabilization at steps 43, 64, 75 and 84 for intervals 1–4. These and the new dispersion values supplement the retained results.

T1.justification: The assumptions, theorem statements, bounds and proofs are substantively unchanged. The proofs in v1 Appendices A–C move to v2 Appendices C–E; the new empirical analysis supplies no additional formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same sparse-weight recovery contribution for shallow scalar-output ReLU networks and the same claims about IHT's performance and memory advantages over IMP.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly associates high variability with empirical phase transitions and interprets poor fitting under infrequent updates as delayed sensing-matrix stabilization. It suggests support stabilization as a stopping criterion. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B documents the added diagnostic experiment's dimensions, sparsity, random initialization, iteration budget and update schedule. Existing implementation details, hardware information and code access remain unchanged after the methods section moves to Appendix A.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to sparse training, convex neural networks and IHT are retained. Expanded author names and other bibliography-format changes do not introduce different research sources.

P1.justification: The experimental-methods section moves from the main text to Appendix A, with a condensed overview added to the results section and a new Appendix B. Most existing prose is retained; affiliations and acknowledgments are also updated.

P2.justification: V2 adds two diagnostic tables and five figures pairing new standard-deviation heatmaps with repeated mean results. Figures 1–5 retain their plots but move within the document. The conference template also changes title styling, headings, running headers and figure placement throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical transparency by exposing variability across the existing three trials and providing focused evidence for the practical update schedule. These additions help readers assess reliability and convergence behavior. The overall gain is limited: the central theory, method and principal comparisons remain unchanged.
